summary: V2 Talent Development + Candidate Comparison tested end-to-end. Backend: new pytest suite /app/backend/tests/test_talent_v2.py (33 cases across competencies, frameworks, employees, employee-mappings upsert, skill-gap analyzer, development plans, candidate compare, multi-tenant isolation, auth) => 33/33 PASSED. Frontend: Playwright drove the full ordered flow on the public preview URL (login -> sidebar -> create framework w/ auto-balance -> create employee -> map current/target -> analyze skill gap -> create dev plan -> candidate multi-select compare + job filter). All flows worked. No functional defects found; 3 minor/cosmetic observations reported below. Test data created during the run was cleaned up from MongoDB.

minor.issue: An assessed competency with gap=0 (already at/above required level) is still labelled priority 'Low' rather than something neutral like 'None'/'Met'. Cosmetically it reads as an outstanding action item. _priority() returns 'Low' for score 0.

employee_id / framework_id are not validated against the org's employees/frameworks (unlike /employee-mappings and /skill-gaps/analyze). A plan can be created with a bogus employee_id and returns 200.

Duplicate ids in candidate_ids cause a false 404 (len(docs) != len(candidate_ids)) instead of de-duplicating; also the >6 guard runs before dedup. Low impact (UI cannot send duplicates), but the error message is misleading.

integration_issues.issue: No client-side cap at 6 selections. Compare button only disables below 2; with >6 candidates in an org the user can select 7+ and will hit a raw backend 400 toast. Suggest disabling additional checkboxes / capping at 6 with a hint.

issues: 'Learning Recommendations' label is truncated to 'Learning Recommendatio…' in the 64px-wide nav (no tooltip/title attribute).

Preview-only React console warning: 'In HTML, <span> cannot be a child of <option>' — caused by the Emergent visual-editor instrumentation wrapping dynamic option text in <span style=display:contents>, not by app code. Informational only, but it does pollute the console on every render of these two pages.

action_items: Optional: validate employee_id/framework_id on POST /api/development-plans (404 when not in org).
Optional: cap candidate comparison selection at 6 in the Candidates UI instead of relying on the backend 400.
Optional: return a neutral priority (e.g. 'Met') when an assessed competency has gap 0.
Optional: add title attribute / wider nav for the truncated 'Learning Recommendations' label.
critical_code_review_comments: routes_talent.py: /employee-mappings upsert sets created_by on every update, overwriting the original author. Use $setOnInsert for created_at/created_by.
routes_talent.py: DELETE /frameworks/{id} does not cascade-delete employee_mappings / development_plans referencing it (DELETE /employees does cascade mappings). Leaves orphan mapping docs.

routes_talent.py: only /candidates/compare uses require_perm(); all talent endpoints (frameworks/employees/mappings/plans create+delete) are open to any authenticated org member including viewer/recruiter roles. Consider RBAC perms for talent writes.

routes_talent.py: DEFAULT_COMPETENCIES global ids are 'g:<name>'; if an org creates a custom competency with the same name as a global, GET /competencies returns duplicates and the framework form lists it twice.
DevPlanItemIn.priority is a free-form str with no enum validation, while DevPlanIn.status is validated manually in the handler — move both to Literal/enum for consistent 422s.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of V2 flows (framework create + auto-balance + weight validation, employee create, mapping save/upsert, gap analysis w/ correct math and priority ordering, dev plan creation, candidate compare 2-6 + skill matrix + job filter)

seed_data_creation: POST /api/demo/seed run once on the admin org (3 jobs + 4 candidates) so >=6 candidates existed for comparison — intentionally left in place for the demo org. All TEST_/QA_ frameworks, employees, mappings, competencies, development plans and 7 transient TEST_ signup orgs were deleted from MongoDB after the run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Verified numerically: framework {Technical Depth L5 w34, System Design L4 w33, Ownership L3 w33} with current levels 2/3/1 => readiness 59.8% and priorities Critical/High/Medium sorted correctly; same framework with no mapping => 19.8% and all rows 'Not Assessed' + amber banner + 'No gaps to add to a plan.' toast on Create plan. Backend readiness formula = 100 - sum((gap/5)*weight)/sum(weight)*100. Multi-tenant isolation verified with fresh signup orgs (empty lists + 404 on cross-org GET/DELETE/mapping/compare). Frontend test-id gotcha: SkillGapAnalyzer selects render before /employees and /frameworks resolve, so wait_for_function on option count > 1 before select_option; also label text is CSS-uppercased so match case-insensitively. Run `python /app/backend/tests/cleanup_test_data.py` plus the TEST_/QA_ talent cleanup after suites.
rca_of_the_issue: No defects to root-cause. The three initial pytest failures were test-side issues I fixed: (1) the session-scoped `api` fixture inherits the httpOnly access_token cookie from the admin login, so unauthenticated assertions must use a fresh requests call; (2) my expected readiness value was mis-computed. Backend behaviour was correct in both cases.
